title: Halving-stage initialization
statement: Let $E,B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathcal O$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four query types and each finite Boolean word, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $Q$ be a proposition. Let $\sigma$ be a register state in which every register is at most $B$, and suppose $\sigma.lg+\operatorname{size}(\sigma.n)\le B$. If the procedure, started in the round state with false phase and index $E$, with $n=0$ and $lg=\sigma.lg+\operatorname{size}(\sigma.n)$ and all other registers as in $\sigma$, terminates on every sequence of choices while keeping every register at most $B$, and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds, then the same termination, register-bound, and acceptance property holds when started in the halving-test state with registers $\sigma$.
hypotheses_covered: an oracle with four query types on finite Boolean words
all registers of $\sigma$ are at most $B$
the procedure from the specified round state terminates on every choice sequence, keeps registers at most $B$, and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds
replaced:
Let $E,B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathcal O$ be an oracle assigning a Boolean answer
to each of four query types and each Boolean-list input, let $x$ be a Boolean list, and
let $Q$ be a proposition. For any register state $\sigma$, suppose every register is at
most $B$ and $\sigma.lg+\operatorname{size}(\sigma.n)\le B$. If, from the generator’s
round state with false phase and index $E$, with $n=0$ and
$lg=\sigma.lg+\operatorname{size}(\sigma.n)$ and all other registers as in $\sigma$,
every computation terminates with registers bounded by $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$
holds, then the same semantic property holds from the halving-test state with registers
$\sigma$.
